name: WWCE Community Fund
summary: Small grants for Wiltshire community and voluntary groups whose projects support wildlife conservation, climate mitigation, carbon reduction or fuel poverty relief, with a panel deciding awards several times a year.

steps: Standard grant application or small grant application

eligibility.rule: Have charitable aims and apply for a charitable project
Have a formal governing document, a management committee and a bank account
Have relevant insurance and a basic Health and Safety policy
Project does not start before the grant decision
Not a commercial company, statutory body, or group promoting political or religious aims
Past recipients must have their previous funded project successfully evaluated before reapplying
No grants or loan schemes run by third parties, or general appeals

documents: Constitution, governing document or set of rules
Most recent annual accounts, or last year's income and expenditure and current budget
Safeguarding Policy and GDPR/Data Protection Policy, if separate
Health and Safety Policy or Risk Assessment

calls.label: Community Fund applications
calls.note: Funding round meetings in 2027 are scheduled for 19 April and 18 October; applications need to be received at least two weeks prior.

status.quote: The fund is currently open for applications and the panel meet twice a year to decide awards.

administered_by.quote: The Community Fund is managed by a Community Fund Panel and administered by Wiltshire Wildlife Trust.

applicant_types.quote: Grants have been allocated to a range of community and voluntary group across Wiltshire

geography.quote: To be considered for funding, the objectives of your Wiltshire-based project should reflect WWCE's own aims.

access.quote: Projects seeking up to £5000 can apply using our grant application form

window.quote: The fund is currently open for applications and the panel meet twice a year to decide awards.

amount.quote: Projects seeking up to £5000 can apply using our grant application form

effort.quote: Projects seeking up to £5000 can apply using our grant application form, while those in need of a smaller boost of up to £500 can use our small grants application form.
Completed applications are shared with members of the Panel who meet several times a year to consider each application, score them against the specified criteria and come to a decision.

eligibility.quote: the applicant's aims and the project for which the grant is applied for must be charitable.

Applicants must have a formal governing document (a constitution or a set of rules), a management committee (however named) being a group of people taking responsibility for the applicant’s actions and use of funds and a bank account.
Applicants must have a Safeguarding Policy.
Relevant insurance such as liability insurance is also required and basic Health and Safety policy.
Projects that have started before the grant application has been determined
Commercial companies Statutory organisations or the direct replacement of statutory funding Political groups or activities promoting political objectives Religious groups promoting religious beliefs
An applicant that has previously received a grant, can apply to the Fund again following successful evaluation of the project granted an award.
Grant or loan schemes run by third parties; Individuals (unless sponsored by a qualifying group or organisation) General appeals

after_award.quote: Groups receiving grants must report on their projects when completed.

documents.quote: Constitution / governing document / set of rules for your organisation b) Annual accounts - the most recent that are available. If you don't have these, please show us your income and expenditure for the last year and your current budget. c) Safeguarding Policy and GDPR/Data Protection Policy (if separate).
Health and Safety Policy or Risk Assessment.
Evidence that you have insurance for your activity or organisation.
